items.heading: Abhyanga (oil massage)
details: Regular massage can promote relaxation and reduce perceived muscle discomfort.

items.heading: Champi (head and scalp oil massage)
details: Scalp massage can promote relaxation, and the oils used can reduce scalp dryness.

items.heading: Tongue scraping (Jihva Nirlekhana)
details: Removes the coating on the tongue and can reduce oral odor.

items.heading: Neem datun
details: Mechanical brushing action removes plaque, and neem itself contains antimicrobial compounds.

items.heading: Traditional chewing-stick tooth cleaning
details: The mechanical action of chewing on a fibrous stick can remove plaque when done correctly.

items.heading: Oil pulling (Gandusha)
details: May reduce some oral bacteria and plaque, but should not replace brushing and fluoride toothpaste.

items.heading: Nasya (nasal oil application)
details: Nasal oil can help moisturize nasal passages; claims of systemic "detoxification" are not established.

items.heading: Traditional steam inhalation
details: Warm, humid air can temporarily ease nasal congestion, though it does not cure the underlying infection.

items.heading: Haldi Doodh (turmeric milk)
details: Provides nutrition and turmeric's bioactive compounds; best regarded as a traditional food rather than a proven treatment.

items.heading: Kadha (herbal decoctions)
details: Provides plant-derived bioactive compounds, though effectiveness depends heavily on the ingredients, dose, and condition.

items.heading: Jeera / Ajwain digestive preparations
details: Traditional preparations built around aromatic compounds associated with digestive comfort.

items.heading: Dinacharya (daily routine)
details: A traditional structured daily routine; regularity of daily activities can support behavioral and circadian consistency.

items.heading: Applying Tilak or Bindi on the forehead
details: The spot between the eyebrows - the "third eye" or Ajna Chakra - is considered a major nerve center point.
Pressing it is believed to improve blood supply to the facial region and promote calmness and focus.

items.heading: Fasting (Vrat / Upavas)
details: Abstaining from food periodically is believed to give the digestive system a much-needed break.
Occasional fasting is associated with improved metabolism and better mental clarity.

items.heading: Wearing toe rings (Bichiya) by married women
details: In reflexology, a nerve passing through the second toe is believed to connect to the reproductive organs.
A snug silver ring on this toe is thought to gently massage the nerve, and silver is also naturally antimicrobial.

items.heading: Applying Henna (Mehendi)
details: Henna paste has natural cooling properties, useful during high-stress occasions like weddings.
Traditional henna also carries mild antiseptic properties, useful before events involving a lot of hand contact.

items.heading: Wearing bangles
details: The constant, gentle friction at the wrist is believed to increase blood circulation to the hands.
Traditionally made of glass or metal, bangles also doubled as a portable, wearable form of savings.

items.heading: Wearing a nose ring (Nath)
details: Ayurveda links a specific piercing point on the left nostril to reproductive health.
The gold or silver traditionally used was also chosen for its believed antimicrobial properties at the piercing site.
